header.title: Breadcrumbs
header.description: Shows the path from home to the current page, so people know where they are and can go back to a previous level with one click. Use it above the title on pages that are several levels deep, like a product detail or a settings screen. It renders a `<nav>` with an ordered `<ol>` list.

playground.title: Playground
playground.description: Tweak the props and see the result and the code instantly. With the long trail and `maxItems` you can see how the middle levels collapse.

base.title: Basic usage
base.description: Pass the path in `items`, from the top level to the current one. Each item needs an `id` and a `label`. The last one is the current page: it's highlighted, it isn't a link and it gets `aria-current="page"`. An item with `href` renders as an `<a>`; without `href`, as a `<button>`. In your app, use `href` with each level's URL.

current.title: Current page in the middle
current.description: By default the current page is the last item. With `current` you can mark another one, for example when the trail also shows the following levels. Items after the current one are still links.

icons.title: With icons
icons.description: `icon` adds an icon before the text. It's decorative (`aria-hidden`), so the text has to work on its own. Use it sparingly: one icon on the first level is usually enough.

separator.title: Separator
separator.description: `separator` replaces the arrow between levels with any node: text like `"/"` or an icon. The separator is decorative and screen readers ignore it.

collapsed.title: Long trails
collapsed.description: When the trail has more items than `maxItems`, the middle ones hide behind a three-dot button that opens a menu. `itemsBeforeCollapse` and `itemsAfterCollapse` set how many stay visible at the start and the end; the button counts as one more slot. The menu closes with Escape, an outside click or choosing a level.

sizes.title: Sizes
sizes.description: `size` changes the text size: `sm` (12px), `md` (14px, default) or `lg` (16px). Use `sm` in tables or dense panels and `lg` in large headers.

navigation.title: Navigate with onItemClick
navigation.description: `onItemClick` receives the chosen item and the one that was the current page before the click. Use it to navigate with a router or to log the move. Here the trail is cut down to the chosen level. Each item also accepts its own `onClick` with the same arguments.

mobile.title: Small screens
mobile.description: The trail wraps onto another line when it doesn't fit the available width, and each level is truncated with an ellipsis past 16rem. On small screens, use `maxItems` to show only the start and the last levels, and `size="sm"` to save space. These boxes simulate a phone width.

header.title: Breadcrumbs API
header.description: API reference for the Breadcrumbs React component: props, items, CSS classes, CSS variables, tokens and exported types.

demos.title: Demos
demos.description: For examples and usage details, visit the component demo page.

import.title: Import
import.description: You can import it from the main entry or from its subpath.

inheritance.title: Inheritance
inheritance.body: It accepts the <nav> HTML attributes (HTMLAttributes<HTMLElement>) and passes them to that element, including ref. classNames adds classes to each part: root, list, item, link, current, separator and overflow.

a11y.title: Accessibility
a11y.landmark: The root is a <nav> with navLabel as its aria-label, so screen readers announce it as navigation.
a11y.list: Levels live in an ordered <ol> list, which announces the number of levels and each one's position.
a11y.current: The current page is a <span> with aria-current="page", not a link.
a11y.overflow: The hidden-levels button has aria-expanded, aria-haspopup and aria-controls pointing to the menu. Its name is overflowLabel.
a11y.escape: With the menu open, Escape or an outside click closes it.
a11y.disabled: Disabled items render as <button disabled> and can't be activated.
a11y.labels: navLabel and overflowLabel default to English ("Breadcrumb", "Show more path"). Pass translated values if your app uses another language.

cssClasses.title: CSS classes
cssClasses.description: Classes you can use to override styles.

rules.root: The `<nav>` element. Receives `className` and `classNames.root`. Defines the Breadcrumbs variables.
rules.size: Applied based on `size`. Sets the text size.
rules.list: The `<ol>` list. Wraps when it doesn't fit.
rules.item: Each `<li>` with its separator and link.
rules.link: Link or button of a previous level. Truncated with an ellipsis past 16rem.
rules.overflow: Container of the hidden-levels button and menu.
rules.trigger: Three-dot button that opens the menu.

cssVariables.title: CSS variables
cssVariables.description: They're defined on `.gem-breadcrumbs` and none are written inline, so you can change them from your own class (`.gem-breadcrumbs.my-class`) or with Tailwind utilities.

items.--gem-shadow-focus: Focus ring of links and the button.

types.title: Exported types
types.description: Available from @gem-org/gem-system to type your own wrappers.

props.title: Props
props.description: It also accepts the HTML attributes of the `<nav>`.

items.items: Trail levels, from the top one to the current one.
items.separator: Node between levels. An arrow by default.
items.maxItems: Number of items above which the middle ones collapse.
items.itemsBeforeCollapse: Visible items at the start when the trail is collapsed.
items.itemsAfterCollapse: Visible items at the end when the trail is collapsed. Minimum 1.
items.overflowLabel: Accessible name of the hidden-levels button.
items.onItemClick: Called when a level other than the current one is chosen. Receives the chosen item and the previous current one.

items.label: Level text. Accepts any node.
items.href: Target URL. With `href` it renders an `<a>`; without it, a `<button>`.
items.current: Marks this level as the current page. Defaults to the last one.
items.disabled: Dims it and it can't be activated.
items.onClick: Called when this level is chosen. Receives the item and the previous current one.
